title: Norm inequality under symmetrization
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X,X':\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have the same distribution and be independent, and let $q\in[0,\infty]$ satisfy $1\le q$. Suppose $X\in L^q(\mu)$ and $\int X\,d\mu=0$. Then for every $a\in\mathbb R$, $\|a+X\|_{L^q(\mu)}\le\|a+X-X'\|_{L^q(\mu)}$.
hypotheses_covered: $1\le q$ for an extended nonnegative exponent $q$
replaced: Let $X,X^{\prime}$ be independent identically distributed real random variables on a probability space, let $1\le q\le\infty$, assume $X\in L^q$ and $\E X=0$, and let $a\in\bbr$. Then $\|a+X\|_q\le\|a+X-X^{\prime}\|_q$, with the essential supremum at $q=\infty$.
